messages.text: The Eureka 16" Blue Ocean Raised Relief Globe is a desktop model — its gyromatic base sits on a table or desk rather than the floor, and the 16" sphere gives you plenty of room to read place names and feel the raised relief detail. Is this one for a home office desk, or more of a display spot like a bookshelf?
looking for similar to eureka but without gyroscopic meridian

The National Geographic Nicollet 16" Illuminated Desk Globe is a good match — same 16" blue ocean size for the desk, but it sits on a simple stand rather than a gyromatic mount, and it adds illumination so you get the glowing terrain map at night. It runs $409.78, a bit more than the Eureka, but you get the National Geographic cartography and lit relief map as a bonus. Want me to point you to that one, or are you looking to stay closer to the Eureka's price point?
i don't need illumination, and something a bit less than $400 would be nice
Searched the catalog · 16 inch blue ocean desk globe metal stand no illumination

The National Geographic Hudson 12-inch Blue Ocean Desk Globe fits well — same blue ocean cartography and raised relief, but it sits on a simple walnut base with a fixed semi-meridian instead of a gyro mount, and it comes in at $160. It's a size smaller than the Eureka (12" vs 16"), but the National Geographic accuracy and walnut hardwood base give it real presence on a desk. Want me to point you to that one?
no. I really want a 16" (or at leat 14")
Searched the catalog · 16 inch blue ocean desk globe semi-meridian stand

I checked closely, and at 16" the only blue ocean desk globes we carry use the gyromatic or full-swing meridian mount — that rotating frame is actually part of what makes a 16" sphere easy to tilt and view at every angle. The Eureka 16" Blue Ocean Raised Relief Globe is $234.75, well within your range, with the gyromatic base built right into its stable black metal stand. Would you like to go with that one?
does the eureka show latitude/logitutde lines?

The product listing doesn't specifically call out latitude/longitude gridlines on the Eureka — it highlights the 4,000+ place names, raised relief terrain, and the gyromatic meridian that lets you rotate and angle the globe freely. For exact confirmation on printed lat/long lines, I'd suggest checking the product photos on the Eureka 16" Blue Ocean page, or reaching out to (email hidden) so we don't guess on that detail.
is shipping free in Canada for this globe?
Shipping within Canada is a flat rate of $10.00 CAD on all orders — but you'll get free shipping if your order totals $99 or more, so the Eureka at $234.75 qualifies for free shipping.

Here's what our Refund & Return Policy page states:

- **Change of mind:** Returns are accepted within 30 days of your order date if the item is unused, in original packaging, with the retail box intact and all accessories/manuals included.
- **Restocking fee:** A 20% restocking fee applies to change-of-mind returns, deducted from your refund (e.g., a $200 globe would be refunded $160).
- **Return shipping:** Returns go through us — once approved, we send a prepaid return label, and its cost is deducted from your refund.
- **How to start:** Email (email hidden) with your order number and reason before sending anything back; items returned without authorization aren't accepted.
- **Damaged/defective items:** Covered by a one-year manufacturer's warranty (90 days for electronics). Contact us within 48 hours of delivery with photos — no restocking fee applies, and we cover replacement/refund plus return shipping.
- **Cancellations:** You can cancel within 24 hours of placing the order by emailing us.
- **Non-returnable:** Custom orders, clearance/final sale items, and gift cards.

Full details: [Refund & Return Policy](https://replogleglobes.ca/pages/refund-return-policy)
